# Requirements Document ## Introduction The contributions-and-resources spec delivers two single-page, YAML-driven sections of matthewfield.ca: 1. **`/contributions`** — a single page rendering curated open-source contributions as cards. Each card shows the upstream repo identity, what Matthew contributed, a short description, the contribution date, and one or more typed links (PR, commit, issue, or release notes). Data lives in `content/contributions.yaml`. No per-contribution subpages. 2. **`/resources`** — a single page rendering curated bookmarks/links grouped by category (e.g. "DevOps Tools", "Blogs & Feeds", "Reading"). Each entry is title + URL + short description. Data lives in `content/resources.yaml`. No per-entry subpages. Both pages are statically generated server components. Both data files are processed by **new Velite collections** (`contributions` and `resources`) that this spec adds to `velite.config.ts`. Both are content-typed (TypeScript types are generated by Velite and consumed at the page level via the `#site/content` chokepoint already established by site-foundation). After this spec ships, Matthew can add or update either section by editing the corresponding YAML file in his editor, committing, and letting CI redeploy — no React changes required. **Explicitly in scope at launch**: - Two YAML data files: `content/contributions.yaml` and `content/resources.yaml`. - Two Velite collections (`contributions`, `resources`) using `s.yaml()` as the entry type, with full schema validation. - Two route files (`/contributions/page.tsx`, `/resources/page.tsx`) — server components, statically generated, no client JS beyond what Next.js's layout pulls in. - Cards for contributions (no subpages, no detail routes). - Category grouping and intra-category ordering for resources. - Empty-file handling: both YAML files MAY be empty arrays; pages render an empty-state message rather than 404. - Inclusion in the existing XML sitemap (via Next.js `sitemap.ts`) and `/sitemap` HTML page. - A pinned authoring contract documented at `docs/contributions-and-resources-authoring.md` covering frontmatter conventions, category enum, and link-type semantics. - Two `src/lib/` helpers — `src/lib/contributions.ts` and `src/lib/resources.ts` — owning queries, sorting, grouping, and validation-error helpers. Page components SHALL import from these helpers only, never from `#site/content` directly. **Explicitly out of scope at launch (deferred to later specs or future enhancements)**: - **Per-contribution detail subpages**: out of scope. Cards are the only surface. - **Per-resource detail subpages**: out of scope. - **Search or filtering UI**: out of scope. Pagefind indexing of `/contributions` and `/resources` is enabled via the existing `data-pagefind-body` convention (blog-enhanced spec), but the pages do not render a search input. - **Tags or cross-linking between contributions and projects/posts**: out of scope. The spec does NOT introduce a `tags` field on either collection. - **External link health-checking in CI** (`lychee`, `linkinator`): out of scope at launch; the link checker step established in blog-core / blog-enhanced naturally covers these pages once they're published, but this spec does NOT add a new CI step. - **A `draft` flag on either collection**: out of scope. Authors curate by editing the YAML directly; nothing is "draft-published-to-prod-but-hidden". If an entry shouldn't ship, it shouldn't be in the YAML. - **An "updated" timestamp on individual entries**: out of scope. Both files are git-versioned; meaningful history is in `git log`. - **Pagination**: out of scope. The expected entry counts (low tens, growing slowly) fit on a single page without pagination. - **Sort controls / user-selectable ordering**: out of scope. Order is schema-defined. - **OpenGraph share images per page**: out of scope; both pages use the site default OG image from site-foundation. - **RSS feed for contributions**: out of scope. - **Importing contributions automatically from GitHub** (via API or scraping): out of scope. Curation is manual — that's the point of a "curated" gallery. - **Resource voting, comments, or external submission form**: out of scope. Resources is a personal bookmarks list, not a community-curated directory. ## Alignment with Product Vision - **Builder credibility** (business objective #2): The contributions gallery surfaces tangible open-source work — repo + PR + description — without forcing visitors to dig through GitHub profiles. - **Personal expression / curated reference** (business objective #3 and product feature #6): Resources is Matthew's curated reading + tooling list, including a "Blogs & Feeds" blogroll category. - **Markdown-first / data-first content** (product principle #2): Both pages are data-driven from YAML files Matthew edits. React renders structure; it never owns repo names, URLs, or descriptions. - **Simple to maintain** (product principle #3): A new contribution is an entry in `contributions.yaml` + commit. A new resource is an entry in `resources.yaml` + commit. No CMS, no admin UI, no per-entry mdx file. - **Independence from platforms** (business objective #4): Contributions are hosted on matthewfield.ca with links back to upstream — even if a forge disappears, the contribution narrative survives in the YAML. - **Wide and spacious** (product principle #1): Card grid for contributions; clean section-grouped list for resources. Both use generous whitespace within the existing site container. - **Responsive** (product principle #6): Contribution cards reflow from multi-column on desktop to single-column on mobile. Resources groups stack vertically at every breakpoint; intra-group entries always single-column for scanability. - **Accessible** (product principle #7): Both pages use semantic landmarks (`
`, `
` with accessible names, `

` per group/card-title), keyboard-navigable links, sufficient color contrast in both themes, and meaningful alt-equivalent text for any non-decorative icons. - **Performance** (success metric #4): Static generation, zero client JS beyond layout, no images on either page at launch (deferred to a future enhancement). ## Requirements ### Requirement 1: `contributions` Velite collection **User Story:** As Matthew, I want to add an open-source contribution by appending an entry to `content/contributions.yaml`, so that the contributions gallery card appears after the next CI deploy with no React changes. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The Velite configuration (`velite.config.ts`) SHALL define a new collection named `contributions` with `pattern: "contributions.yaml"`, `single: false` (the file's top-level is a list of entries — Velite handles list-of-entries-from-one-file via array-shaped schema). The existing `pages`, `profile`, and `posts` collections SHALL remain unchanged. The collection registration SHALL be additive — no rename, no behavioral change to other collections. 2. The schema for each `contributions` entry SHALL require: - `repo` (string, 1–80 chars; format `owner/name`, validated by regex `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*\/[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$`) — the upstream repo identity. - `repoUrl` (string, URL-parseable, `http:` or `https:` only) — canonical URL of the upstream repo (e.g. `https://github.com/owner/name`). - `title` (string, 5–100 chars) — short description of the contribution (PR title, "Added X to Y", etc.). - `description` (string, 30–280 chars) — one- or two-sentence narrative of what the contribution was, why it mattered, or what Matthew learned. - `date` (ISO 8601 date — when the contribution landed/merged; if not yet merged, the submission date). - `links` (array of typed link objects — see Req 3; minimum 1 entry, maximum 6). 3. The schema for each `contributions` entry SHALL support these optional fields: - `language` (string, 1–24 chars) — primary language of the upstream repo, used as a textual badge on the card (e.g. "Rust", "TypeScript"). - `summary` (string, 60–200 chars) — explicit social/SEO summary override. **Out of scope at launch**: per-card OG images. This field exists for future use but is NOT rendered or consumed by route metadata at launch. 4. WHEN the build runs AND any entry violates the schema THEN the Velite build SHALL fail with a named error citing the offending entry (by `repo` if present, else by array index) and the field. Failure cases include: missing required field; invalid datetime; string length out of bounds; invalid URL or non-http(s) scheme; invalid `repo` format; unknown frontmatter key under `.strict()`; invalid `links[]` entry (Req 3); empty `links` array; `links` array with more than 6 entries. 5. The schema SHALL use `.strict()` mode — typos like `repoUrl:` written as `repoURL:` or `repo_url:` SHALL be build errors. 6. WHEN `content/contributions.yaml` does NOT exist OR exists with explicit content of `[]` (empty list) THEN the Velite build SHALL succeed and emit `contributions: []`. The page handles the empty array gracefully (Req 2.7). 7. The Velite output type for `contributions` entries SHALL be generated and surfaced via `#site/content`. Direct `JSON.parse` of `.velite/contributions.json` outside `src/lib/contributions.ts` is prohibited (enforced by the same lint/test convention used for projects). 8. **Order-of-operations**: The schema definition, the data file (with at least an empty-list placeholder if no real entries exist), and the route file SHALL land in the SAME commit (or a sequence where every intermediate commit leaves CI green). ### Requirement 2: `/contributions` gallery page **User Story:** As a visitor, I want to land on `/contributions` and see a card-style gallery of Matthew's open-source contributions. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. WHEN a visitor navigates to `/contributions` THEN the page SHALL render a reverse-chronological grid of contribution cards, sorted by `date` descending, with `repo` ascending as the tiebreak. The comparator `byDateDescRepoAsc` lives once in `src/lib/contributions.ts`. 2. WHEN the page is rendered THEN it SHALL be a statically generated server component with `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`. 3. WHEN the page is rendered THEN each card SHALL include, in DOM order: - The `repo` string rendered as plain text in a heading element (`

`) with stable `id="contrib-"`. The heading is the card's primary semantic title. - The `title` (PR/contribution title) rendered as a sub-heading element (`

` with appropriate visual weight; NOT a heading per HTML spec because each card has only one heading level — the repo). - The `description` paragraph. - The `date`, formatted via `formatContentDate(iso)` from the existing `src/lib/format-date.ts` module. - A `language` textual badge iff `language` is present. - A typed-link rail (Req 3) rendered as inline link chips/buttons, NOT as a sentence with embedded anchors. 4. **No nested anchors / no whole-card-as-link**: each card is a `

` element. The links inside the rail are independent `` targets. The card itself is NOT a single anchor, because each card has multiple distinct external link destinations (PR + commit + repo, etc.) and choosing one as "the card link" would obscure the others. 5. **Card link semantics**: every external `` inside a card SHALL have `rel="noopener"` and SHALL render same-tab (no `target="_blank"`). Middle-click or Cmd/Ctrl-click for new tab. This matches the policy from the project-showcase spec. 6. WHEN the page is rendered THEN its `` SHALL be "Contributions" composed through the site-foundation `%s | matthewfield.ca` title template. Meta description is a short author-curated string in the page component. OG image MAY be the site default. 7. **Empty state**: WHEN `contributions` is `[]` THEN the page SHALL render a polite empty-state message ("No contributions published yet." or similar) rather than 404 or a blank page. 8. **Responsive breakpoints**: WHEN viewport <640 px THEN single-column. WHEN 641–1023 px THEN two-column. WHEN ≥1024 px THEN at least two-column; finer escalation is a design-phase concern. 9. **Pagefind**: the cards container SHALL be wrapped (or otherwise marked) so that the Pagefind crawler from blog-enhanced indexes the contribution text without indexing site chrome. This SHALL follow the existing `data-pagefind-body` convention from blog-enhanced, not invent a new one. ### Requirement 3: Typed-link rail on contribution cards **User Story:** As a visitor reading a contribution card, I want to find the PR, commit, issue, or release-notes link in one predictable place, with a clear indication of what each link points to. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The `links` field on each contribution entry SHALL be an array of objects of shape `{ kind: "pr" | "commit" | "issue" | "release" | "discussion"; label?: string; url: string }`. - `kind` (required; CLOSED ENUM — only the five literal strings above; any other string is a build-time error). - `url` (required) — validated per Req 3.3. - `label` (optional, 1–60 chars). When omitted, the rendered text is the `kind`'s default label (e.g. `kind: "pr"` renders "PR #1234" if the URL is a recognizable GitHub PR URL, else "Pull request"; design-phase finalizes the default-label table). 2. **Uniqueness per kind**: at most ONE entry per `kind` value per contribution. Authors with two of the same logical type (e.g. two related PRs) SHALL list them as separate top-level contributions or include only the primary one. Build error on duplicate `kind` within a single entry. 3. Each entry's `url` SHALL be validated in two stages: (a) `new URL(url)` parse — invalid is a build error; (b) protocol check — only `http:` and `https:` are accepted; all other schemes are rejected with a named error citing the contribution entry and the link's array index. 4. **Display order is array order**. Authors choose link prominence by reordering the array. 5. **At least one link is required** (per Req 1.2). A contribution with no link is not a contribution worth listing. 6. **Link attributes**: every link in the rail SHALL render with `rel="noopener"` and same-tab. No per-link override. Same as Req 2.5. 7. The rail SHALL be server-rendered. Each link is a plain `<a>`. ### Requirement 4: `resources` Velite collection **User Story:** As Matthew, I want to add a bookmark by appending an entry to `content/resources.yaml`, so that it appears under its category on `/resources` after the next CI deploy. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The Velite configuration (`velite.config.ts`) SHALL define a new collection named `resources` with `pattern: "resources.yaml"`. Like `contributions`, this is one file containing a list of entries. The collection registration SHALL be additive. 2. The schema for each `resources` entry SHALL require: - `title` (string, 2–80 chars) — the resource's display name. - `url` (string, URL-parseable, `http:` or `https:` only). - `description` (string, 20–200 chars) — short why-this-matters note. - `category` (string — CLOSED ENUM at the schema level; canonical category list pinned in the schema. Initial set: `devops-tools`, `blogs-and-feeds`, `reading`, `fun-stuff`. New categories require a schema update. Rationale: a closed enum prevents typos creating new "categories" with one entry each.). 3. The schema for each `resources` entry SHALL support these optional fields: - `added` (ISO 8601 date — when this resource was added to the list; used as a secondary sort key within category — see Req 5.3). Default: absent. WHEN `added` is absent for any entry within a category, that entry sorts AFTER entries with `added` set, preserving its declared array order among other absent-`added` entries. 4. WHEN the build runs AND any entry violates the schema THEN Velite SHALL fail with a named error citing the offending entry (by `title` if present, else by array index) and the field. Failure cases include: missing required field; invalid URL or non-http(s) scheme; string length out of bounds; unknown frontmatter key under `.strict()`; invalid `category` (not in enum). 5. The schema SHALL use `.strict()` mode. 6. WHEN `content/resources.yaml` does NOT exist OR exists with explicit content of `[]` THEN Velite SHALL succeed with `resources: []`. The page handles this gracefully (Req 5.6). 7. The Velite output type SHALL be surfaced via `#site/content`. Direct `JSON.parse` is prohibited outside `src/lib/resources.ts`. ### Requirement 5: `/resources` page **User Story:** As a visitor, I want to land on `/resources` and see Matthew's curated bookmarks grouped by clear categories, with each entry presenting a title, link, and short description. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. WHEN a visitor navigates to `/resources` THEN the page SHALL render entries grouped by `category`, with category sections in the canonical order defined by the closed enum from Req 4.2 (`devops-tools`, `blogs-and-feeds`, `reading`, `fun-stuff`). Display labels for each category (e.g. "DevOps Tools", "Blogs & Feeds") are author-curated and live in `src/lib/resources.ts`, NOT in the YAML. 2. WHEN the page is rendered THEN it SHALL be a statically generated server component with `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`. 3. **Intra-category order**: within a category, entries SHALL sort by `added` descending (most recently added first), with `title` ascending as the tiebreak. Entries WITHOUT `added` sort AFTER entries WITH `added`, preserving their YAML-declared order among themselves. Comparator `byAddedDescTitleAsc` lives once in `src/lib/resources.ts`. 4. WHEN the page is rendered THEN each category section SHALL include, in DOM order: - A category heading (`<h2>`) with the display label and stable `id="cat-<category-slug>"`. - A list (`<ul>`) of entries; each entry is a `<li>` containing: the title as a link (`<a>` with `href=url`, `rel="noopener"`, same-tab) and the description as adjacent text. 5. Categories with zero entries SHALL NOT render a heading or an empty list — they are silently omitted. Authors don't need to remove categories from the enum just because they're currently empty. 6. **Empty state**: WHEN `resources` is `[]` THEN the page SHALL render a polite empty-state message. No 404. 7. WHEN the page is rendered THEN its `<title>` SHALL be "Resources" composed through `%s | matthewfield.ca`. Meta description is a short author-curated string in the page component. OG image MAY be the site default. 8. **Pagefind**: the entries region SHALL be wrapped per the `data-pagefind-body` convention. 9. **Responsive**: category sections stack vertically at every breakpoint. Within a category, entries are always single-column (a scannable bulleted list, not a card grid). 10. **In-page nav (anchor links)**: AT LAUNCH, the page SHALL NOT render a sticky table-of-contents or floating in-page nav. Each category heading SHALL still have a stable `id` (Req 5.4) so external deep links (e.g. `/resources#cat-reading`) work. A TOC component is a future enhancement, gated on whether the page grows enough to need it. ### Requirement 6: Sitemap inclusion **User Story:** As a search-engine crawler, I want both `/contributions` and `/resources` listed in the XML sitemap. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The existing `src/app/sitemap.ts` SHALL include `/contributions` and `/resources` as static URLs, alongside the existing `/`, `/profile`, `/projects`, `/blog`, etc. 2. The HTML sitemap page (`/sitemap`, owned by the slash-pages spec) SHALL list both pages once it is implemented. **This spec does NOT modify `/sitemap`** — that integration is the slash-pages spec's responsibility. This spec only updates `sitemap.ts` (the XML sitemap). 3. `lastModified` for each entry MAY be derived from the most recent `date` (contributions) or `added` (resources) of any entry on that page, OR from a static build-time timestamp. The exact value is a design-phase concern; the requirement is that the entry exists. ### Requirement 7: Helper modules **User Story:** As a future maintainer (Matthew himself or an agent), I want each content type's query / sort / display-label logic in one obvious place, so I can change ordering or category names without grepping route files. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. `src/lib/contributions.ts` SHALL export: - `getAllContributions(): ReadonlyArray<Contribution>` — returns the Velite-typed array, already sorted by `byDateDescRepoAsc`. Page imports from here, NOT from `#site/content` directly. - `byDateDescRepoAsc(a, b)` — the comparator (Req 2.1). - Type re-exports for `Contribution` and `ContributionLink` from the Velite-generated types. 2. `src/lib/resources.ts` SHALL export: - `getAllResources(): ReadonlyArray<Resource>` — Velite-typed array. - `getResourcesGroupedByCategory(): ReadonlyArray<{ category: ResourceCategory; label: string; entries: ReadonlyArray<Resource> }>` — pre-grouped, pre-sorted by `byAddedDescTitleAsc` within group, and category order matching the canonical enum order. Groups with zero entries are omitted. - `byAddedDescTitleAsc(a, b)` — the comparator (Req 5.3). - `RESOURCE_CATEGORY_LABELS: Record<ResourceCategory, string>` — the enum-to-display-label map (Req 5.1). - Type re-exports for `Resource` and `ResourceCategory`. 3. **Test coverage**: both helpers SHALL have unit tests (`*.test.ts` colocated, matching the pattern set by `src/lib/blog.test.ts` and `src/lib/projects.test.ts`). Tests cover: sort comparator behavior; group-omission of empty categories; correct fall-back behavior for missing-`added` entries (Req 5.3). 4. **`#site/content` chokepoint**: neither route file (`/contributions/page.tsx`, `/resources/page.tsx`) SHALL import from `#site/content` directly. The existing eslint rule pattern from site-foundation (the one that exempts `src/lib/*.ts`) SHALL be extended to apply to `src/lib/contributions.ts` and `src/lib/resources.ts` as legitimate consumers. (If the existing rule is "anything in `src/lib/` may import"; no rule change is needed — verify in design.) ### Requirement 8: Author-facing documentation **User Story:** As Matthew authoring contributions or resources later, I want a single doc that tells me the YAML shape, the available link kinds, and the available resource categories, so I don't have to re-read the Velite config. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The spec SHALL produce `docs/contributions-and-resources-authoring.md` covering: - The contributions YAML shape (required fields, optional fields, the `links[]` typed-link table, the `kind` enum, the `repo` format). - The resources YAML shape (required fields, optional fields, the `category` enum, the `added` semantics). - How sort order works on each page. - The empty-file behavior. - The "no draft flag" policy. - One concrete example entry for each collection. 2. A build-time check (lightweight, similar to `checkProjectHeadings` for projects) SHALL verify that the doc still contains each expected section heading (e.g. "## Contributions YAML shape", "## Resources YAML shape", "## Link kinds", "## Resource categories"). Missing section heading → build warning, NOT error. The intent is to surface drift, not to over-couple. ### Requirement 9: Cross-spec wiring (landing page, /slashes index, nav) **User Story:** As the site's owner, I want the existing hero-card landing-page treatment and the slash-pages index (when it ships) to include `/contributions` and `/resources` so visitors discover them, without re-architecting the data layer. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. The landing page hero cards SHALL include cards for `/contributions` and `/resources`. **If the existing hero-card data structure already lists these as placeholder routes** (per the site-foundation decomposition note about data-driven hero cards), no schema change is needed — only the placeholder is replaced with the real route. If not, this spec adds them. 2. The top-nav (header) SHALL include direct links to `/contributions` and `/resources`, OR they SHALL be reachable from one click on the landing page. The exact placement (top-nav vs. landing-only) is a design-phase concern; the requirement is "discoverable in one click from `/`". 3. **/slashes index integration** is OUT OF SCOPE for this spec — `/contributions` and `/resources` are NOT slash pages (they are major sections, not /-prefix IndieWeb conventions). The slash-pages spec SHALL NOT add them to the `/slashes` index. ### Requirement 10: Lifecycle and editorial workflow **User Story:** As Matthew editing either YAML file, I want predictable failure modes when I make a typo, and predictable rollback when an entry turns out to be wrong. #### Acceptance Criteria 1. **Typo → build fail**: every kind of schema violation is a CI-blocking build error, surfaced with the file and entry identifier (Req 1.4, Req 4.4). No silent skipping. 2. **Renaming a contribution / resource**: there is no concept of "the URL of an entry," because neither page has per-entry subpages. Renaming has no SEO consequence — the entry's `title` / `repo` changes, but no route changes. No redirects needed. 3. **Removal**: removing an entry from the YAML SHALL remove it from the page on the next deploy. No tombstone, no redirect. 4. **Rollback**: a wrong commit is rolled back by `git revert`. There is no per-entry "unpublish" flag. 5. **No draft state**: an entry is either in the YAML (published next deploy) or not. Authors working on an entry locally can hold it in a feature branch. ## Non-Functional Requirements ### Code Architecture and Modularity - **Single Responsibility Principle**: `src/lib/contributions.ts` owns contribution queries; `src/lib/resources.ts` owns resource queries. Page route files own only rendering + metadata. Velite config owns schema definition and entry-level validation. - **Modular Design**: The contributions schema, the resources schema, the typed-link helper, and the empty-state behavior are each independently testable. - **Dependency Management**: Page route files MAY import from `src/lib/contributions.ts`, `src/lib/resources.ts`, `src/lib/format-date.ts`, shared UI primitives, and Next.js. Page route files MAY NOT import from `#site/content` directly. - **Clear Interfaces**: All public exports from `src/lib/contributions.ts` and `src/lib/resources.ts` SHALL be typed; comparators SHALL be `(a, b) => number` matching the existing convention in `src/lib/blog.ts` and `src/lib/projects.ts`. ### Performance - Both pages are statically generated at build time. Zero client JS is added by this spec beyond what the existing site layout already includes. - No images on either page at launch (deferred). No layout-shift risk. - Lighthouse performance target: 90+ on both pages, verified manually at launch. ### Security - All external links carry `rel="noopener"`. - All external URLs are validated at build time (`new URL()` parse + http/https-only protocol check) in both collections. No `javascript:`, `mailto:`, `data:`, etc. - No user input is ever rendered (these are author-curated YAML files committed to git). No XSS surface beyond the existing site CSP. ### Reliability - Empty YAML files / `[]` payloads SHALL NOT break the build. Both pages render an empty-state message. - A schema violation is a build error with a clear identifier, not a silent skip. - A failed CI deploy SHALL NOT leave the previous production build broken — the existing Vercel rollback flow covers this and requires no spec-specific work. ### Usability - Cards and category sections are keyboard-navigable in source order. - Color contrast targets WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes. - Both pages render correctly in dark and light themes (visual verification at launch). - `/contributions` and `/resources` are reachable from the landing page hero cards in one click. ### Maintainability - The category enum on resources is intentionally closed — adding a category requires editing the schema, NOT just typing a new string in YAML. This prevents typo-driven "ghost categories" containing one entry each. - The link-kind enum on contributions is similarly closed for the same reason. - The authoring doc (Req 8) is the single source of authoring truth; the schema is the single source of validation truth. Both live in version control.
